verdict: The report's measurement layer is extraordinarily good and the Babele-mechanics layer is essentially sound — build on both. Every headline number I recomputed from the dumps matched to the character: 74 actors / 523 items / 137 tables / 1,530 results / 151 pages / 13 journals / 15 scenes / 49 folders / 5 macros; special.value 30/81,617; notes 45/40,265 with 38 HTML; comment.value 307/99,697; general.comment.value 100/19,595; modifiers 19,493 across exactly 30 paths; notes '[object Object]' x267/4,005; journal text 2,230,280; result descriptions 163,191; result names 806/9,925; macro commands 9,347; actor prose exactly 130,003; 38 duplicate ranges (37 core / 1 starter); embedded sources 144 world + 36 dead-pack = 180/180; and the headline expose:true coverage 155/180 (86.1%) and 48,181/52,998 (90.9%) reproduce exactly, uncovered set and all. I also independently confirmed the load-bearing Babele claims in source: `expose` is a real DocumentConverter param (document-converter.js:60-62,152) and the publish actually reaches sibling and nested fields because MappedCompendium builds ONE DocumentTranslationScope per document and threads it through prepare and map (mapped-compendium.js:527-531; document-translation-scope.js:80-85; compendium-runtime.js:55-69 preserves localPacks on child(); embedded-compendium.js:26 does the localMappedCompendiumFor lookup); `_when` supports all/any/equals/in/exists exactly as used (mapping-block.js:176-206); variant fields shadow base fields by key exactly as described (mapping-block.js:126-140); registered mappings MERGE with built-ins so the inherited Item/Actor `description` defaults do survive (document-mappings.js:267-287,347-361); the functional-converter signature `(value, translation, source, contextCompendium, allTranslations, runtime, params)` is correct (functional-converter.js:44-53); `registerMapping`/`registerConverters` really are babele.init-only (babele.js:197-199, 291-293, 984-993); `_sourceCollection` really does require a `^Compendium.` prefix (document-converter.js:539); the default Item/Actor/JournalEntry/TableResult mappings really are dead against this system; and the eleven hard-coded RollTable names, the two folder-name lookups with no null check, the 'None' sentinel at actor.mjs:2493 and the skill-stunts `game.items.getName(skill.description)` lookup chain all check out at the cited code. What you cannot take on trust is the third layer — the per-field characterizations and the proposed JS. The JS ships one dead variant (`crit-inj` should be `critical-injury`), one converter that is pure cost (`alienTokenName`), and a half-applied guard policy that leaks alien-only keys into every other system's exports; and several DO-NOT-TRANSLATE verdicts are right for the wrong stated reason (modifiers labels are not derived at all, header.type.value is not '0'/'1'), which means the reasoning cannot be reused when the data changes. Practically: treat the counts, path inventory, coverage math, risk list and Babele mechanics as verified; re-derive every "the values are X" sentence and every line citation before quoting it; fix the `critical-injury` key, drop `alienTokenName`, add `exists` guards to the non-description variants, add the 36 @TEXTDRAW/@DRAW labels to the table-name sync surface, and read Babele's importAdventure/syncImportedAdventureTokenNames hook before touching prototypeToken.name or Scene.tokens.
